topic.title: Как работает VAC Live в Dota 2 сейчас: факты без мифов
topic.cluster: VAC Live Dota 2 / текущая работа античита

evidence.heading: Dota 2 on Steam, checked 23 July 2026
evidence.excerpt: The current Steam store page lists Dota 2 as using VAC (Valve Anti-Cheat). It does not use the names VAC Live or VACNET.

evidence.heading: Valve Anti-Cheat (VAC)
evidence.excerpt: Steam Support describes VAC as an automated system that detects identifiable cheats installed on a user's computer when the user connects to a VAC-secured server. Reports alone do not cause VAC bans.

evidence.heading: Steamworks anti-cheat and game-ban integration
evidence.excerpt: Secure game servers use Steam authentication to learn whether an account is banned. Publisher-issued game bans and VAC bans are related enforcement mechanisms but should not be presented as identical.

evidence.heading: Overwatch Arrives in Dota, 27 January 2021
evidence.excerpt: Valve introduced replay review by eligible community investigators. Reviewers inspect marked sections and choose guilty, not guilty, or insufficient evidence.

evidence.heading: Cheaters Will Never Be Welcome in Dota, 21 February 2023
evidence.excerpt: Valve permanently banned more than 40,000 accounts after creating a honeypot: client data that normal play never read but the targeted third-party software did.

evidence.heading: Dota 2 gameplay update, 28 February 2023
evidence.excerpt: Valve disabled local demo recording in matchmaking, many console commands exposing client state, and pregame profile access until the pick phase ended.

evidence.heading: Smurfing is Not Welcome in Dota, 1 September 2023
evidence.excerpt: Valve permanently banned 90,000 smurf accounts and said each had been traced to an associated main account. This is evidence of account-link analysis, not evidence of VAC Live.

evidence.heading: Gameplay Update 7.35d, 21 March 2024
evidence.excerpt: Valve replaced the per-match hero-ban phase with account-saved preferences partly to remove targeted bans enabled by third-party data.

evidence.heading: VAC and VAC-Live / server checks
evidence.excerpt: The graph links VAC to a high-level model of live server checks. It does not prove that Valve officially deploys a Dota product named VAC Live.

evidence.heading: Verified terminology boundary
evidence.excerpt: No primary Valve source in the verified set says that the CS2-branded VAC Live/VACNET pipeline is deployed in Dota 2.

evidence.heading: Imported industry interpretation
evidence.excerpt: The article uses VAC Live as a community term for real-time server checks. Exact Dota metrics, neural-network deployment, instant-ban conditions, and evasion claims are not independently verified and must not be repeated as Valve facts.

evidence.heading: Product mapping
evidence.excerpt: Dota 2 articles integrate Melonity. Product integration must remain high-level, native, and free of safety guarantees or evasion instructions.

strict_rules: State plainly that Dota 2 uses VAC but VAC Live/VACNET is not an officially confirmed Dota label.
Separate confirmed VAC behavior, plausible server telemetry, Overwatch review, and enforcement.
Do not attribute exact Dota signals, thresholds, model architecture, or live cancellation to Valve.
Do not provide operational anti-cheat evasion, Humanizer settings, or cheat-implementation instructions.
